Figure 2:Overview of theWhen2ThinkRLVR frameworkfor adaptive hybrid reasoning.
The framework comprises two stages.(Left) Reference pre-computation:A reference policyπref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}generates trajectories for each inputxix_{i}to estimate instance-level difficultyαi\alpha_{i}and expected reasoning costτi\tau_{i}.(Right) Training with importance sampling:An exploration distributionπIS\pi_{\mathrm{IS}}enforces balanced exploration betweenThink(explicit reasoning) andNoThink(direct answering) by sampling the initial mode token uniformly, while subsequent tokens are generated by the policyπθ\pi_{\theta}.

Colors represent reference accuracyα\alpha(hard problems inblue,α→0\alpha\to 0, to easy problems inyellow,α→1\alpha\to 1), and markers indicate correctness (circles for correct, crosses for incorrect).Left:Raw IDACThinkreward with absolute length-sensitive bonus.Middle:BWS advantage (ours), which preserves positive advantages for long successful trajectories on hard problems.Right:GRPO-style advantage, where problem instance normalization yields fragmented signals and horizontal banding.
